wy_citadel_the.blurb: The Citadel is a south-facing sport wall in Sinks Canyon above Lander, standing just left of the Addiction wall. All 19 routes are bolted, and the grading leans hard: a single easy line, a couple of 5.10s, a handful of 5.11s, and a big cluster of 5.12s with two 5.13s on top. The wall is a tall clean panel on the right, broken up by ledges and ramps toward the left. The headline line is The Citadel of Hope, a steep slab leading to a small-holds headwall. Canyon sport climbing here is on dolomite, and the south exposure keeps it warm.

wy_drugs_and_sex.blurb: Drugs and Sex is a sport wall in the Valhalla zone of Ten Sleep Canyon in the Bighorn Mountains, at roughly 7,900 feet. Its 19 routes are all bolted and aimed at strong climbers: one in the 5.10 range, seven at 5.11, nine at 5.12, and two at 5.13. The cliff is compact with a slight lean; the right side offers sustained pockets and crimps while the left side works through a roof. These are long pitches, and several have mid-height anchors, so you can warm up on the lower portion or bail to an easier finish.

wy_scud_wall.blurb: Scud Wall is the go-to moderate cliff on the Sinks Canyon limestone near Lander. All 19 routes are bolted. Most fall at 5.10 and under, with one easy 5.6, a few at 5.7 and 5.9, eight in the 5.10 range, and four at 5.11. Climbs are single pitch on good rock, and the wall faces south so it picks up sun. A small pinnacle sits downhill with a short trad ridge and a few extra sport lines. Expect company, especially on weekends; quieter days are weekday mornings.
wy_scud_wall.approach: Start from the main Sinks parking lot, follow the trail up toward Killer Cave, then continue roughly 100 yards to the right to reach the wall.

wy_honky_tonk.blurb: Honky Tonk is a bolted sport section of the Old Road crags in Ten Sleep Canyon, Wyoming, near the falls at the bottom of the old road. It holds 19 routes, and the grades sit in a narrow band: four at 5.10, nine at 5.11, and six at 5.12. That makes it a good fit for climbers already comfortable at 5.10 to 5.12 who want pocketed canyon face climbing, with the neighboring Powers Wall a short walk away. There is nothing easier here, so beginners will want another sector.

wy_1_fossil_hill_west.blurb: Fossil Hill West is the left-hand end of the Fossil Hill sport complex above Sinks Canyon near Lander, at nearly 9,000 feet. It has 19 bolted routes, starting with a couple of 5.7s and a 5.8, then jumping to a handful of 5.10s and a strong group of 5.11 and 5.12 lines, with three 5.13s at the top end. Well-known lines include Fossil Logic and Channel Zero. It sees less traffic than the central wall, which makes it a quieter pick at the grade.

wy_addiction.blurb: Addiction is a bolted sport wall at the top of the left-hand trail from the main lot in Sinks Canyon, outside Lander. The 19 routes run from an easy 5.7 slab on the left side up to 5.13b, but most of the weight is hard: seven at 5.12 and five at 5.13, plus four at 5.11. The main face is mostly steep with varied holds, while the left end has a few moderate slabs. It faces southeast, so it gets morning sun and falls into shade later in the day, and a few newer, lightly climbed lines can be loose.
wy_addiction.approach: From the main Sinks parking lot, follow the left-hand branch of the trail uphill; the wall is at the top of that branch, above the third campground.
